projects.name: Birana-ብራና
projects.description: Free and first invoicing app for Ethiopian businesses. Amharic and English, Ethiopian and Gregorian calendars, VAT, turnover and withholding tax. Runs entirely in the browser with no backend. Your data never leaves your device. project.

caseStudy.overview: Birana (ብራና) is a free invoicing app for small businesses in Ethiopia. It works in Amharic and English, supports the Ethiopian and Gregorian calendars, handles VAT, turnover tax, and withholding, and runs entirely in the browser, so it works offline and never uploads your data. The name is the traditional Ethiopian parchment that manuscripts were written on.
caseStudy.problem: Small businesses in Ethiopia often make invoices by hand or retype them in Word. That leads to maths mistakes, inconsistent numbering, and no record of who has paid. Most invoicing software assumes English only, the Gregorian calendar, a steady internet connection, and a monthly subscription.
caseStudy.solution: A bilingual invoicing tool that is free. A shop owner can make a correct invoice in about a minute, with tax calculated automatically and dates shown in the calendar their customers use. They can then share it by WhatsApp, Telegram, or email, and track payments.
caseStudy.approach: I started with the constraints: no backend, works anywhere, bilingual, and fast on low-end phones. I built it in phases, with the calculation engine and calendar first, because money and dates have to be right before anything else matters. Each phase had automated tests and was checked in the browser before the next began. After the first redesign looked polished but was hard to use, I reworked it around usability: five main navigation items, a simple editor with advanced options folded away, and a guided Quick Invoice flow for first-time users. I checked the screens at phone, tablet, and desktop sizes, in light and dark themes, and in both languages.
features: Invoices, proforma invoices, and receipts, with automatic numbering and no duplicates
Amharic, English, or both on the same invoice, switched with one tap
Ethiopian calendar (13 months) and Gregorian dates, shown either way or both
VAT, turnover tax, or no tax per invoice, plus optional withholding, with editable rates
Payment tracking with part payments and automatic overdue status
Sharing through WhatsApp, Telegram, or email with ready-made reminder messages
Quick Invoice mode: a 3-step guided flow
decisions: Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, no frameworks or dependencies. The app stays small and fast on low-end phones and slow connections. There's no build step and nothing third-party to break or review. No backend. Data lives in the browser's local storage. This protects privacy and removes server costs. The trade-off is that data doesn't sync across devices, so I added backup and restore. Money stored as integer cents. This prevents the rounding errors that floating-point numbers cause when adding tax and discounts. Ethiopian calendar written from scratch using Julian Day Numbers, instead of a library. I could handle leap years and test the conversions myself. Print-to-PDF through the browser's print engine instead of a PDF library. Many libraries render Ge'ez script badly, and the browser's engine handles it correctly. Service worker with network-first caching. The app works offline, but users still get new versions right after an update. Static hosting on Vercel. There's nothing to run on a server, so the site is fast and cheap to host.
challenges: onverting between Ethiopian and Gregorian dates. The Ethiopian calendar has 13 months, and the short last month has 5 or 6 days depending on the year. I built and tested the conversion against known dates and across 20 years of round trips.
Amharic in printed invoices. My first thought was a PDF library, but it couldn't render the script reliably. Using the browser's print engine with a dedicated A4 stylesheet solved it

Recurring invoices without a server. With nothing running in the background, I generate due drafts when the app opens, cap how many are created, and stop generated drafts from creating more. The app says plainly that nothing is sent automatically.

Making it easy to use, not just good-looking. My first redesign was colourful but crowded: too many menu items and too many options on one screen. I rebuilt the layout around fewer choices and measured how many taps the main tasks took.
caseStudy.outcome: Birana is a working, installable invoicing app with no dependencies and no backend, deployed at [your live link]. It has automated tests for money calculations (15), the calendar (13), and recurring invoices (6), and all 444 interface strings exist in both English and Amharic. [Add real results here once you have them, such as how many people tried it, any feedback, or a business that used it. Don't add numbers you don't have.]
caseStudy.learnings:
A tool for a specific market has to start from that market's real habits (language, calendar, tax, phones, connectivity), not from a generic template.
A polished-looking interface can still be hard to use. Counting taps and testing on a real phone showed problems the screenshots hid.
Doing the numbers and dates first, with tests, made everything built on top of them safer.
Choosing not to use a backend or libraries was a design decision: it gave privacy and speed, but I had to plan for backup, offline updates, and the lack of sync.
Honest limits build trust. The app says clearly that it isn't a tax-authority-approved system, and that users should back up their data.
I still need native Amharic review and a tax professional's check before wider use.

projects.name: SmartCV
projects.description: A free, browser-based career toolkit for Ethiopian job seekers to improve CVs, evaluate job compatibility, generate tailored cover letters, track applications, and prepare for interviews.

image.alt: Stylised preview of the SmartCV interface showing a CV builder and compatibility score

caseStudy.overview: SmartCV is a browser-based CV and career toolkit built for Ethiopian job seekers. The repository implements a rules-based layout engine, live CV preview, client-side PDF export, local draft saving, and an Ethiopian payment-gateway integration for optional premium themes.
caseStudy.problem: Many Ethiopian job seekers face difficulties creating professional CVs, identifying suitable job opportunities, and preparing for recruitment processes. Existing career tools can be expensive, require account registration, or are not tailored to local job seekers.
caseStudy.solution: A free, browser-first toolkit that combines CV creation and career preparation in one accessible application, without requiring an account for the core workflow.
caseStudy.approach: Designed and developed SmartCV, a free, browser-based career toolkit that helps Ethiopian job seekers improve their CVs, evaluate job compatibility, generate tailored cover letters, track applications, and prepare for interviews. Focused on creating an accessible, straightforward experience without requiring user registration.
features: Smart Layout Engine that analyzes experience, content density, and skills list length before choosing section order, columns, font scale, and skills display.
Live CV preview while the multi-step form is completed.
Five free visual themes plus three premium themes, with Chapa payment integration for premium unlock.
decisions: Next.js 14 with App Router and TypeScript.
React for building reusable UI components.
Browser-based functionality to minimize infrastructure requirements and avoid mandatory user accounts.
challenges: The default PDF font does not include Ge'ez glyphs, so full Amharic PDF text needs an embedded Ethiopic font.
The free tier single-page limit is enforced in the UI rather than in the PDF renderer.
caseStudy.outcome: Successfully developed and deployed a functional career toolkit at https://smartcv-virid.vercel.app/. The platform brings multiple job-search and career preparation tools together in one accessible application, including CV tools, Job Match scoring, Career Twin, Cover Letter generation, application tracking, interview preparation, and Readiness Cards.
caseStudy.learnings: Building and deploying a complete web application using Next.js and TypeScript; designing practical user experiences around real-world problems; managing client-side application state with Zustand; implementing PDF-related functionality; structuring reusable components and responsive interfaces; balancing functionality, usability, and infrastructure costs; turning a real-world problem into a working software product.

projects.name: Mesob Connect
projects.description: An internal messaging and document management system for formal correspondence, attachments, message tracking, and direct messages.

image.alt: Stylised preview of the Mesob Connect messaging and document management interface

caseStudy.overview: Mesob Connect is an internal messaging and document management system for formal correspondence. The implementation combines a React frontend, Express/Node.js API, MySQL database, JWT and bcrypt authentication, Server-Sent Events, and PDF generation.
caseStudy.problem: Organizations need one place to compose formal letters, manage correspondence, attach documents, and track message status instead of relying on scattered messages and files.
caseStudy.solution: A single internal workspace for formal letters, requests, document attachments, message status tracking, direct messages, and department/user administration.
caseStudy.approach: Developed a full-stack internal messaging system with formal-letter templates, attachment support, inbox/sent/drafts filters, message event history, direct messages, and admin-managed users and departments.
features: Internal messaging with inbox, sent, and drafts views.
Memo and request-letter workflows with formal-letter templates.
Document attachments and authenticated PDF access.
Message status history and event tracking.
User and department management for administrators.

decisions: Separate React/Vite client and Express/MySQL server, matching the repository structure.
MySQL schema with a message status lifecycle and a message_events table to support tracking and audit history.
JWT authentication with admin-created accounts and bcrypt password handling; WebAuthn dependencies are present in the repository.
CORS allowlist, security headers, a 2 MB JSON limit, and 10 MB upload error handling in the server.
Generated PDFs are served only through an authenticated /api/messages/:id/pdf route.
Server-Sent Events were used for live message updates instead of polling.
challenges: Coordinating message status changes, event history, document attachments, and live updates across the client and API.
Protecting generated documents and messaging endpoints with authentication, CORS rules, and security headers.
caseStudy.outcome: A working full-stack system covering correspondence, formal letters, attachments, tracking, and admin management.
caseStudy.learnings: Designing a status-driven data model, separating client and server concerns, and applying auth, CORS, and CSP controls to internal tools.
